notVerified.item: IME composition in a bound Input
notVerified.why: every keystroke writes $state and re-evaluates the whole program, and the field's value is that state; composition events and the candidate window do not exist in jsdom
notVerified.howToVerifyLocally: In a real card, type a two-character Chinese word with a pinyin IME into Input($t, 'Text'). Pass: every character lands, the candidate window is not interrupted, and a sibling Text(@Format(…)) agrees. Fail: a dropped character, a reset composition, or a caret jump.

notVerified.item: A ticking Timer beside a focused Input
notVerified.why: the countdown writes $state once a second, so the whole card re-evaluates once a second; focus and caret behaviour under re-render is a browser property
notVerified.howToVerifyLocally: One card with Timer($s, 'Left') and Input($n, 'Name'). Focus the input, start the timer, type slowly for ~5 s across several ticks. Pass: focus and caret never move and no character is lost. Fail: focus jumps away, the caret resets, or input is swallowed.

Rebuild, then hash the profile's installed lib/ against the build before believing any measurement; pnpm reports 'Already up to date' for a file: dependency while keeping the hard-linked old copy.

notVerified.item: Refresh and history replay for a card whose fields were edited

notVerified.howToVerifyLocally: Type into three fields, reload the page, then reopen the conversation from history. Pass: the values are the ones that were typed, not the program defaults.

defects.summary: The build depended on an optional peer nobody declared (unrun)
defects.detail: tsdown@0.22.14 needs unrun to load tsdown.config.ts and lists it as an optional peer; pnpm does not install optional peers that were never asked for, so install && build failed on every clean machine while working on the developer's.
defects.status: Fixed in chore(build); verified with node_modules deleted

defects.summary: A meta-size assertion measured the temp path, and had never executed
defects.detail: metaBytes < FRAGMENT.length + 600 versus a measured 972; the constant is ~760 (the fragment is stored twice, plus an absolute path and two content addresses). On Windows the test failed three lines earlier, so the assertion had never run on either platform.
defects.status: Replaced with a ratio assertion (metaBytes < FIGURE.byteLength / 50), validated by re-introducing the defect: 205772 vs 4096.32

defects.summary: The first Timer cleanup test passed for the wrong reason
defects.detail: A leaked interval writes into the store it captured, and a reload has already replaced that store, so a value-based remount test stayed green with clearInterval deleted.
defects.status: Cleanup is now asserted by counting pending timers; deleting the cleanup turns two tests red

openQuestions.topic: The persisted meta stores the fragment twice
openQuestions.detail: presentationMeta writes both fragment and the pre-fork source; for a html card nothing reads source (visualizeMetaFrom needs fragment, openuiMetaFrom returns early when fragment is present), so it is 234 bytes a card of dead payload.
openQuestions.whyNotFixedHere: removing it changes the persisted shape and needs an ADR; the benefit is 234 bytes, the risk is historical replay

mutationChecks.purpose: a guard that has never been seen to go red is a guess about what it protects
mutationChecks.M1: delete Timer's clearInterval -> 'pauses without writing' and 'clears its interval when the card goes away' both fail
mutationChecks.M2: append the figure's bytes to the persisted meta -> 'expected 205772 to be less than 4096.32'
